rationale:
Claude faithfully adopted the three round-2 amendments, and the corrected packet implements their core: the placeholder legend separates `

`, ``, ``, and ``; the D-SEAL bytes contain neither `` nor ``; the archive is the tree at ``; `` and `` have exact-delta checks and are pushed in order; rollback is ordered and qualified; the ignored-overlay guard uses `--ignored`; `docs/ARCHIVE.md` is reviewed; and §0.3 now cites the retained round-1 subject `29d7a11c…`. The corrected packet and Claude reply also match their pinned hashes. Adversarial re-reading nevertheless finds inconsistencies outside that repaired core. D-SEAL clause 2 maps citations only in COORD, file 08, and frozen artifacts, while `docs/ARCHIVE.md` and §6.8 say the rule also maps `DECISION-PACKETS/` and the other committed root files. The default condition-5 clause carries the word `reserved` past the very authorization that must precede sealing. Recommended option 6.10(b) creates `docs/DECISIONS.md`, and §4.8 requires an entry there, but the file is absent from the proposed tree and post-move sequence; additionally, final sign-off cannot always be its first entry if a CONTESTED-page disposition was already required. The manifest rule permits regeneration precisely after archive drift, which would re-pin the defect instead of detecting and reverting it. Finally, the packet ties the optional 21 candidate ADRs to §6.3/§6.4 while simultaneously recommending 49 ADRs plus candidate inclusion and calling 128 the recommended baseline; the intended distinction needs to be explicit. Claude's separate `30+` bytecode count is directly refuted by the 29 files on disk at the pinned HEAD. These are bounded amendments, so disagreement with the overall plan is not warranted.
